statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 11 of 100 in the low band, fourteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday is now more than thirty-six hours old and removes the very price path this score measures; thirteen of the twenty-four published forward slots lie inside that closure. Stress holds at 65, the base of the high band, because this hour added confirmation rather than escalation: the Hormuz vessel strike near Qeshm was confirmed with one death and a crew evacuation, while the offsetting diplomatic leg widened with Iraq resuming passenger traffic at its Iranian crossings, an Egypt-Iran leaders' meeting in New Delhi and a reported Monday GCC, Iraq and Iran meeting in Oman on temporary Hormuz shipping lanes. Confidence holds at 86 on a full primary-source re-verification of levels, yields, oil, the event calendar and every published item cited here. Tail stays below the block threshold throughout the closed stretch and reaches the watch band only in the five slots around the scheduled 22:00 UTC restart.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in thirteen of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so there is no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme available to score. Second, the weekend escalation record is severe but is held in Stress rather than Tail, because Tail measures a pathological price path and no path exists to be pathological; the record is also genuinely two-sided this hour, with several concrete de-escalation reports alongside the strikes. Third, the one structural checkpoint inside the horizon is the scheduled restart, and the five watch-band slots from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday are published as a narrow evidence-based danger window rather than a broad shutdown. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this reading.
headline: More than thirty-six hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while Iranian authorities confirm one death and a crew evacuation after a vessel was struck near Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi missiles and drones hit Saudi territory at Sharurah and near Jazan, Iraq has resumed passenger traffic at its Iranian crossings, GCC and Iraqi ministers are reported to meet Iran in Oman on Monday over temporary Hormuz shipping lanes, and market pricing still implies roughly 85 per cent odds of a 25 basis point increase at Wednesday's FOMC.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour rather than carried over. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91 per cent, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the session high, roughly 4.5 per cent under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The last quote is timestamped 11 September at 17:15 New York time. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.84 close, inside a 15.59 to 17.71 range, a notably calm volatility print against this macro backdrop. Rates and oil are equally static: the Federal Reserve H.15 release still carries its 10 September observation at 4.56 per cent for the 2-year, 4.95 per cent for the 10-year and 5.37 per cent for the 30-year, while WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.37 per cent, and Brent at $104.61, down 2.81 per cent, after Friday's rally paused on the Oman talks headline.

The weekend record moved in both directions this hour, and on the whole it added confirmation rather than fresh escalation. On the escalation side, Iranian authorities confirmed that a commercial vessel struck off the Hengam and Qeshm coasts at about 01:30 UTC left one person dead and three wounded, with a fire aboard and crew evacuation reported as the hour opened; UKMTO recorded the vessel as hit by an unknown projectile and advised transits to proceed with caution. Yemen's Houthis claimed drones and missiles against a military base at Sharurah in Saudi Arabia's Najran region, and Saudi civil defence reported a projectile falling near the Yemen border that injured two people and damaged a mosque, while Houthi forces and Yemen's recognised government intensified fighting over the Bab el-Mandeb approaches. Reported drone disruption to Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline matters structurally, because that line is the principal Hormuz bypass.

The offsetting leg is unusually concrete for a weekend. Iraq resumed passenger traffic at its crossings with Iran after Saturday closures, Egypt's and Iran's leaders met in New Delhi with de-escalation urged, the UAE's top diplomat discussed a UAE-Iran leaders' meeting, and GCC and Iraqi foreign ministers are reported to meet Iran in Oman on Monday to discuss temporary Hormuz shipping lanes and mine clearing. No start time has been published for that meeting, so it is excluded from the event list and carried as an untimed headline window in the later forecast hours instead.

Macro framing is hawkish and unresolved. Hot August CPI and PPI prints leave market pricing at roughly 85 per cent for a 25 basis point increase at Wednesday's FOMC, with an implied policy path near 3.84 per cent, an unusual configuration alongside WTI at $100. Under the repository definitions that configuration raises Stress and shapes Confidence; it is not by itself a Tail input. The shared Finviz context file was read as required but is both stale at about two and a half hours old and marked partial with its calendar section unavailable, so it was not relied upon; its futures, megacap and semiconductor rows only restate Friday's session, which independent primary sources already confirm.

The single structural checkpoint inside this horizon is the scheduled 22:00 UTC restart of CME equity index futures. Conditional Tail is published in the watch band for the five hours from that restart to 03:00 UTC on Monday, which defines the danger window, and it stays in the low band everywhere else. Nothing in the closed stretch can be scored as observed structure, and no later slot asserts a price path that has not happened.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 09:00 UTC on 12 September to 08:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window sits entirely inside the CME weekend closure. Tail held at 6 for the first twenty slots, in normal mode and mapped to EA_ON and green throughout, then stepped to 7 at 05:00 UTC, 8 at 06:00 UTC, 9 at 07:00 UTC and 10 in the final slot, tracking the lengthening closure rather than any directional view. Stress described a shallow arc, easing from 57 to a 50 low at 17:00 UTC as Friday's crude pullback and the Oman talks headline were absorbed, then rebuilding through 52, 53, 56 and 57 to 65 by the close of the window as the weekend escalation reports accumulated and attention turned to the restart. Confidence held an 85 to 87 band, its 85 readings early in the window reflecting distance from the last print rather than any loss of verified data. Nothing in the window revises a past opinion with later information.
outlookSummary: Thirteen of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday; the reference contract is scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's fourteenth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 11 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts gradually to 19 through the closure as the interval without price discovery lengthens and unpriced weekend exposure accumulates. It is capped at 19 for the final closed hour, because a market that cannot trade cannot produce the failed retracements the score measures. It then steps to 24 in the restart hour, the top of the watch band, and eases through 23, 22, 21 and 20 as two-way flow is assumed to return, falling back to 19 and 18 across the Asian session before edging to 19 again in the European morning as the untimed Oman headline window opens. Those five watch-band slots define the danger window from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday. Stress eases from 65 to 63 through the quiet Sunday stretch, builds to a 70 peak at the restart on the unresolved two-chokepoint supply picture and thin reopening liquidity, then decays to 65 across the Asian session and firms to 67 by the horizon close as Wednesday's FOMC approaches. Confidence declines from 86 to a horizon low of 80 immediately before the restart as distance from the last verified print grows, then recovers to 86 once a live tape exists again. Mode stays normal through the closure, is published as event/whipsaw for the two restart hours and mixed where cross-asset conflict is plausible.
